transformations.edit: Replaced the seed-only contract/body string recorder with an executable Verus target function, adapting the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &[T]` argument and naming the return.

Attached the generated `len == N`/`Some`/`None` postconditions and the `array_ref_view(ret.unwrap()) == slice@` relation directly to the executable target; this records the contract under test and does not assume the target body.

Preserved the Rust 1.96 branch flow: `if self.len() == N`, then `as_ptr`, pointer `cast_array`, unsafe array-reference cast, `Some(me)`, and else `None`; the implicit receiver is the only source syntax adaptation.

Reused the already verified `core::slice::as_ptr` dependency shape through a local executable `as_ptr` wrapper with `slice_start_ptr`, and isolated only Verus-unsupported `ptr.cast_array()` plus `unsafe { &*ptr }` as named source-backed raw-pointer/array-reference boundaries.
